renamed_or_corrected.evidence: npm view @base-ui-components/react deprecated -> "Package was renamed to @base-ui/react". Both packages share the same description/homepage (base-ui.com) and repository (github.com/mui/base-ui). Handled via a pnpm.overrides alias rather than dropping the name, so any archived source that still imports the literal string "@base-ui-components/react" resolves to the current package's code.

renamed_or_corrected.evidence: @shadcn/react@0.3.0 is a real, currently-published package (repo github.com/shadcn-ui/ui, dir packages/react) but its package.json "exports" map has no root "." entry — only "./message-scroller" and "./questionnaire" subpaths. A bare `import "@shadcn/react"` fails to resolve at build time; archived code must import a specific subpath. Package itself is legitimate and was kept as a dependency.

overrides_added.reason: Deprecated/renamed upstream (see renamed_or_corrected). Aliasing keeps the old import specifier resolvable against current, maintained code instead of installing the abandoned 1.0.0-rc.0.

@react-three/postprocessing@3.0.5 declares a peer requirement of three>=0.182.0. Because three is pre-1.0, a caret range on 0.180.0 only allows patch bumps (0.180.x) and cannot satisfy that peer. Bumped the constraint to the nearest range that clears the peer check; verified with `pnpm install` that the peer-dependency warning for @react-three/postprocessing disappeared afterward.

Archive spans 5 registries built at different times against React 18 and React 19; several packages (e.g. some @radix-ui/*, react-aria-components, chakra-ui ecosystem deps) still list react/react-dom ^18 in peerDependencies alongside ^19. pnpm's default behavior only warns (does not hard-fail) on peer mismatches, but this makes that lenience explicit and reproducible instead of relying on default CLI flags, and lets auto-install-peers pull in any missing shared peers (e.g. @types/react for peer-optional cases) without manual chasing.

overrides_added.override: pinned to ^3.8.0 (archive declared both recharts@3.8.0 and recharts@2.15.4 from different registries)
overrides_added.reason: A single package.json can only carry one version of a bare 'recharts' import. Picked 3.8.0 (newer major) for better React 19 compatibility. Components authored against the 2.15.4 API may see behavioral/type differences at runtime — this is a known, recorded gap rather than a silent drop; recharts itself installs successfully either way.

overrides_added.override: pinned to ^0.542.0 (archive also had a bare 'lucide-react' entry with no version)
overrides_added.reason: Chose the explicit archived constraint over the unconstrained one to match the icon set/API most components were built against (latest major is 1.31.0, a breaking jump).

overrides_added.override: pinned to ^4 (archive also had a bare entry)
overrides_added.reason: Honored the explicit archived constraint over resolving to whatever 'latest' would give unconstrained.

overrides_added.override: pinned to ^8.0.0 (archive also had a bare entry; npm's current latest major is 9.x)
overrides_added.reason: Archived components were written against the v8 API; installing v9 would resolve but likely break call sites. Honored the explicit archived constraint; pnpm printed an informational '(9.1.2 is available)' notice, not an error.

pnpm 10 blocks postinstall/build scripts by default for supply-chain safety, which left esbuild's native-binary postinstall unrun and vite non-functional. Explicitly allow-listed esbuild's build script (the only one needed here) rather than disabling the protection globally.
